This application has been preferred seeking condonation of delay in filing the application for restoration being CRAN 2 of 2025.

2. Having heard the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and upon perusal of the averments made in paragraphs 6 to 17 of the application explaining the delay, I am satisfied that sufficient cause existed which prevented the petitioner from filing the application for restoration within the prescribed period of limitation.
3. Accordingly, the application for condonation of delay being CAN 3 of 2025 is allowed.
CRAN 2 OF 2025 4.

Having heard the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and perused the averments made in the application, I am satisfied with the explanation offered regarding the absence of the learned Advocate on 09.01.2023, when the revisional application was taken up for hearing.

5. Accordingly, in exercise of the power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (corresponding to Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) and in the interest of (Binodilal Agarwal & Anr vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr.) on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53856329/
1 justice, the order dated 09.01.2023 is hereby recalled.
6. The application for recall being CAN 2 of 2025 is thus allowed.
7. The revisional application being CRR 1102 of 2014 is restored to its original file and number.

sentences.text: The present revisional application has been preferred challenging the legality and propriety of the order dated 28.02.2014 passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Bench-II, City Sessions Court, Bichar Bhawan, Calcutta, in Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2013, affirming the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated P age |2 22.04.2013.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Judge, Bench-II, City Sessions Court, Bichar Bhawan, Calcutta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner was convicted for the commission of an offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and to pay a fine of Rs. 2,000/-, in default of payment, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one year.
9.
Mr. Chattoraj, learned Advocate representing the petitioner, submits that the complaint on which the case being O2 D of 2011 was initiated against the petitioner was lodged in the year 2011.

Referring to the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the Act of 2006),
he submits that in view of the provisions of Section 97 of the Act of 2006, all the Acts referred to in the schedule appended to the Act of 2006 have been repealed.
He further submits that the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was incorporated in the schedule of the Act of 2006.
Referring to the Notification dated 29.07.2010, he submits that the effect of Section 97 of the Act of 2006 was to be given to from the date of publication of that Notification, i.e., 29.07.2010.

Therefore,
according to him, on the date of initiation of the proceeding, the enactment, namely the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, was not in force, and consequently, the authority proceeded against the petitioner under a repealed enactment.
He submits that this issue was raised before the Trial Court as well as before the Appellate Court; however, both courts have overlooked this issue and arrived at an erroneous finding.
He submits that the petitioner has a fair chance to succeed in this revisional application.
10. He submits that the present petitioner no. 1 is seriously ill and almost bedridden, and if the order of sentence is not suspended, the petitioner shall suffer serious prejudice.

11. Having heard the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and upon perusal of the materials on record, I am of the view that the issue raised in this revisional application warrants consideration on merits, and the petitioner has made out a prima facie case.
12. In view thereof, the order of sentence dated 22.04.2013 is suspended until the end of December 2025 or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
13. The petitioner is directed to serve a fresh notice upon the opposite parties intimating that this matter shall be taken up for further consideration on 25.11.2025.
